title: natsel architecture
description: From genes in code to species at the edge and back through events

blocks.title: Skills and CI/CD
blocks.description: Genes live in code; SDK registers them

children.title: natsel skills
children.description: Create genes by contract, delete or fix them
children.details:
LLM skills act as codemods that follow the **gene contract**: one locus, no dependency on other genes, mechanical removal.

- **create** a gene with several alleles
- **delete** a losing gene (a PR)
- **fix** a winning gene: merge into the base and remove the flag (a PR)

A human approves every PR.

children.title: Build-time registration
children.description: SDK sends the gene list to the Control Plane
children.details: At build time the SDK collects the list of genes and sends it to the Control Plane. **Code is the source of truth**: a gene exists only if it is in the code.

children.title: Gene registry
children.description: Assigns each gene a position in dna
children.details: Positions of extinct genes are not reused while old cookies live; a new epoch starts with a new `dna` version.

children.title: Weights
children.description: Thompson sampling by niches, under constraints
children.details: Traffic weights come from species metrics. Manual control is expressed as **constraints** (max share, ramp-up, segments, forbidden combinations), never as weight edits, so the statistics stay valid.

children.title: Gene statistics
children.details: Fitness is scored **per gene**, by regression over species genotypes. Interactions are modelled only within a locus. Low score → extinction, consistent win → fixation.

blocks.title: Breeder at the edge
blocks.description: Picks a species, writes dna to a cookie
blocks.details:
Sits in front of the CDN. Takes weights from the Control Plane, picks a species for a **new** user and writes its `dna` to a cookie. A returning user keeps their species; they are reassigned only when it goes extinct.

`dna` is a signed (HMAC) bit record: `version | gene field 1 | gene field 2 | …`. A bad signature means reassignment. Hundreds of genes fit in tens of bytes.

blocks.title: CDN and app
blocks.description: dna in the cache key; SDK enables genes
blocks.details:
The CDN includes `dna` in the cache key, so the cache splits by the number of species, not users.

The SDK makes no requests at runtime: it enables genes from `dna`. Unknown bits are ignored and a gene without a bit runs its default, so rolling back a build is safe.

blocks.title: Event pipeline
blocks.details: Exposures (`dna` + the gene that actually fired) and outcome events, on top of your existing analytics (warehouse-native). A **fast guardrail path** kills a lethal species within minutes.
